title: Building Reliable Agentic Systems: Eno Reyes
talk_summary: Eno Reyes of Factory describes agentic systems as planning + decision-making + environmental grounding, and gives practical techniques from building their 'droids' (code review, docs, coding agents). Key actionable ideas: hardcoded explicit plan criteria, feedback-processing layers for noisy logs, custom AI-computer interfaces for recurring tool chains, and bounded exploration before starting a task.

takeaways.technique: Explicit feedback processing layer for CI/logs
takeaways.evidence_quote: I know the llm is going to want the failing tests so let me get the failing tests and also provide a brief like explainer of what the rest of the logs were doing

takeaways.technique: Explicit plan criteria / hardcoded success states
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately keep hardcoded logic and explicit success criteria for plans rather than relying on generalizability, validating plans with hard-coded checks and few-shot examples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: clearly defining kind of successful structures or at least successful initial States for plans uh can lead to like very strong kind of Downstream effects

takeaways.technique: Custom AI-computer interfaces for recurring tool chains
takeaways.what_they_do: When a fixed multi-step tool sequence recurs (calculator -> parse logs -> transform), they build a single dedicated tool/interface instead of making the agent re-derive the chain each time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how can we build this tool and then build the interface to the llm for this tool so that you can kind of streamline those types of uh actions

takeaways.what_they_do: Allow agents a longer upfront context-gathering phase, then force a transition into execution; the right bound must be found empirically via evaluation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at a certain point you need to kind of say let's jump into the problem and what we found is that finding the right balance of bounded exploration time is very difficult

takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate subtask outcomes and current state during execution and replan based on real-time feedback, especially when humans or environment change mid-run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evaluating outcomes of your subtasks and your current state uh and enabling kind of adaptive replanning based on real-time feedback

takeaways.what_they_do: Run multiple inferences and select the best sample via clustering or voting; accuracy rises with more samples but costs more and adds latency unless parallelized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the more inference at run time that you run and the more that you can like build a clever way of selecting ideal or optimal samples ... the higher the accuracy
